entries.tagline: Remove background noise from voices
entries.summary: Cleans up hiss, hum and room noise while keeping the voice clear. Good for rescuing recordings made in noisy places.
useCases: Clean up a phone recording
Reduce fan or air-conditioner noise
Make interviews clearer
howTo: Select a clip with audio on the timeline
Open the Inspector
Choose Remove noise
Compare before and after, then apply

entries.tagline: Everyday effects to fix and style your clips
entries.summary: A big library of effects for correcting color, blurring, adding glow or glitch, removing green screens and retouching faces. Some effects use depth to relight a scene or blur the background, which works best with the Depth add-on.
useCases: Fix exposure, tint and saturation on a dull clip
Blur or glow parts of a shot
Remove a green screen background
Smooth skin and add subtle makeup
Add a glitch or warp for a stylish moment
howTo: Select a clip on the timeline
Open the Effects panel and browse or search for an effect
Click an effect to add it to the clip
Adjust its sliders in the Inspector

recommends.reason: Unlocks 3D relighting, background blur and fog

entries.tagline: Funny face effects that follow faces
entries.summary: Finds faces in your clip once, so warps and other face effects stay locked on as people move.
useCases: Add funny face warps to a vlog
Retouch faces consistently through a clip
Make playful reaction videos
howTo: Select a clip with faces on the timeline
Open the Effects panel
Add a Funny face effect
Let Drift scan the clip, then adjust

entries.tagline: A small AI assistant that runs on your computer
entries.summary: A language model that lets the local agent read and edit your open project. Everything stays on your computer, no account needed.
useCases: Ask the assistant to make edits for you
Work without sending your project online
Experiment with an AI helper offline
howTo: Open the Agent panel
Choose the local model
Type what you want done to your project

requires.reason: Runs on the local agent runtime

entries.tagline: Find moments by what is in the shot
entries.summary: Looks at each scene and names the people, animals, vehicles and objects in it. Lets you search and rank scenes by what they contain.
useCases: Find every shot with a dog
Sort scenes by what appears in them
Pick the best clips from long footage
howTo: Select a long clip on the timeline
Open the Scenes tool and detect scenes
Run scene labels
Search or filter the scenes by what you want

entries.name: AI Engine — Processor (CPU)
entries.tagline: The AI engine that works on every computer
entries.summary: Powers Drift's AI tools such as captions, cutouts and noise removal. It runs on your computer's processor and is installed automatically the first time an AI tool needs it.
useCases: Required by every AI tool in Drift
Works on any computer, no special graphics card needed
howTo: Pick an AI tool and install it; the engine is added automatically
Nothing else to set up

entries.tagline: Upscale and clean up low-quality video
entries.summary: Sharpens and enlarges footage with models made for anime, live action and 3D animation, and cleans up compression and noise. Choose the model that suits your footage.
useCases: Upscale old or low-resolution clips
Clean up blocky compressed video
Sharpen anime and cartoons
howTo: Select a clip on the timeline
Open the Enhance video tool
Pick a model and preview it
Run it to create the enhanced clip

entries.tagline: Cut people out of the background automatically
entries.summary: Removes the background behind people with no clicking, keeping soft edges so hair looks natural. Works across a whole clip.
useCases: Replace or blur the background without a green screen
Put text behind a person
Make a quick cutout for a thumbnail or overlay
howTo: Select a clip with a person on the timeline
Open the People cutout tool
Run the cutout and preview the result
Place something behind it or apply effects

entries.tagline: Turn speech into captions automatically
entries.summary: Listens to your clip and writes subtitles for what is said, in about 99 languages. Captions appear on the timeline ready to edit and style.
useCases: Add subtitles to an interview or vlog
Transcribe a talk to edit by text
Make videos accessible and easier to watch muted
Translate your workflow by starting from an accurate transcript
howTo: Select a clip with speech on the timeline
Open the Captions panel
Choose Create captions from speech
Edit the generated lines if needed

entries.tagline: Exact word timing for English captions
entries.summary: Pins each spoken English word to the moment it was said. Cuts and captions land between words instead of in the middle of them.
useCases: Cut by editing the transcript text
Word-by-word highlighted captions
Cleaner cuts between sentences
howTo: Create captions from speech on an English clip
Open the Captions panel
Refine word timing, or edit the transcript to cut
The better timing is used automatically

entries.tagline: Describe sounds and search clips by sound
entries.summary: Tags what you can hear, such as applause or rain, and finds moments that match a sound you describe. Helps you search and sort media by how it sounds.
useCases: Find the applause in a long recording
Search for a whoosh or rain sound
Rank clips by how well they match a sound
howTo: Select a clip or section
Open audio analysis
Ask for sound tags or search for a sound
Jump to the matching moments

entries.tagline: Understand depth for lighting and focus
entries.summary: Works out how far away everything in a shot is. This lets effects add lights that fall on the scene, blur the background realistically, add fog or place titles behind people.
useCases: Blur the background like a real camera lens
Add fog that gets thicker with distance
Light a scene from a new direction
Put text behind a person
howTo: Select a clip on the timeline
Open the Effects panel
Add a depth effect such as Depth of field
Let Drift analyze the clip, then adjust the effect

unlocks.label: Depth fog and titles behind people

entries.tagline: Eye-catching looks for short videos
entries.summary: Effects made for social clips, such as sparkle, beat shake, kaleidoscope and lightning. Also includes ready-made effect templates that move with the beat of your music.
useCases: Make a clip pop on a short-form video
Shake or flash the picture on the beat
Add sparkle or lightning to a highlight
Start from a ready-made effect template
howTo: Select a clip on the timeline
Open the Effects panel and look for the Trending effects
Add one to your clip
Adjust it in the Inspector, or pick a template to apply several at once

entries.tagline: The engine that runs the local assistant
entries.summary: A small program that runs a language model on your computer's processor, so the local agent works without a graphics card. Installed automatically when needed.
useCases: Required by the local assistant model
howTo: Install it together with an assistant model

entries.name: AI Engine — NVIDIA CUDA
entries.tagline: Faster AI on NVIDIA graphics cards

Run any AI tool as usual

entries.tagline: Cleaner people cutouts for difficult shots

Final-quality cutouts
howTo: Open the People cutout tool on a clip
Pick the Best quality option
Run the cutout and wait for it to finish

entries.name: Sound Type Detection

useCases: See where the music starts and stops

Name the sounds in a recording

Run the analysis

entries.name: AI Engine — AMD ROCm (MIGraphX)

entries.tagline: Click a subject and cut it out of a clip

entries.tagline: Over a hundred ways to move between clips

entries.name: Speed boost — WebGPU (any graphics card)

entries.summary: Makes AI features faster using an AMD, Intel or NVIDIA graphics card, with no extra toolkit to install. It adds to the AI engine you already have.

entries.tagline: 21 good-looking fonts for titles and captions

entries.tagline: Faster AI with Windows ML on any DirectX 12 graphics card
entries.summary: The same AI features, sped up by any modern graphics card (AMD, Intel, NVIDIA or Qualcomm) with nothing else to install. On Windows 11 24H2 and newer, Windows adds vendor-tuned speedups by itself, and Drift falls back to the processor if the card can't be used.
